image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Begin gently straightening the held plug, translating to roughly preserve its tip position and retaining the existing grasp.
Continue small rotational alignment above the slot; keep the plug centered while reducing the visible gap slowly.
Finish straightening in small increments with tip-pivot compensation; nudge the plug toward the socket center while still above it.
The plug appears laterally centered and nearly vertical. Lower it a few millimeters while maintaining orientation and the existing grasp.
Approach the socket entrance slowly with the plug centered; preserve the grasp and watch for contact or misalignment.
The plug tip is at the socket entrance. Advance gently downward while keeping the current alignment and grasp.
Continue a slow, straight insertion; the tip appears centered at the slot, but seating is not yet confirmed.
Advance another millimeter slowly along the slot axis, preserving alignment and grasp; seating remains visually uncertain.
Continue a small axial seating motion while retaining the grasp; the connector is at the socket, but full insertion is not yet clear.
Make another small straight seating motion, keeping the plug aligned and the grasp unchanged; full insertion remains uncertain.
Use a smaller final axial advance while watching the connector at the socket; keep the existing grasp and orientation.
Make a very small seating advance, then pause with the grasp unchanged. The socket interface is partly occluded, so seating is not confirmed.
Hold the current alignment briefly to let the connector settle; the occluded interface does not yet establish full seating.
Try a further half-millimeter axial seating motion without changing the grasp; the tip remains centered visually but the interface is occluded.
Use a very small axial advance, then settle; the plug meets the slot visually, but the occluded contact does not confirm seating.
Try a submillimeter depth-alignment correction with minimal downward motion; the plug is centered laterally, but its seating remains occluded.
Refine alignment along the camera-depth direction without further downward pressure; compare the plug with the fixed slot after this small correction.
Lift five millimeters to inspect the plug/socket relationship; the visible plug base has stopped descending, so avoid continuing to press without checking alignment.
The plug lifted with the hand and remains above the slot. Re-approach gently with a small depth correction, retaining lateral alignment.
Back off slightly and correct the camera-depth alignment toward the slot center before another insertion attempt; keep the connector grasped.
Re-approach the visible slot at the corrected depth with small axial steps, preserving the retained connector and watching the entrance.
Lower gently at the corrected alignment. The connector remains over the slot; watch whether the body seats as the fingers approach the socket surface.
Continue a gentle axial insertion at the current centered alignment, monitoring the connector body rather than assuming seating from hand motion.
Try one millimeter of controlled axial seating at the corrected alignment. The socket masks the tip, so inspect the connector's motion before further adjustment.
The connector base appears stationary despite descent. Lift to clear the entrance and reassess depth and angular alignment rather than pressing further.
Clear the lip slightly and shift the plug tip about two millimeters away from the camera, with a small pitch correction before re-approaching.
Approach at the newly adjusted depth and pitch, stopping short of the visible socket lip to check alignment before seating.
Lower the retained plug toward the entrance at the revised alignment, using a short descent to check whether its base follows the hand.
Close the small visible gap at the revised alignment with a 1.25 mm descent, watching whether the connector follows rather than assuming insertion.
Make a submillimeter depth correction and gentle seating advance; the housing is close to the socket surface, so avoid a large push.
Clear the socket lip and shift slightly toward the camera to test depth alignment; repeated downward motion has not visibly seated the plug.
Adjust the plug's pitch slightly with tip-pivot compensation and move its tip toward the camera about 1.5 mm, then approach the socket gently.
Refine depth alignment slightly away from the camera while making a short, gentle axial insertion at the corrected pitch.
Apply only a small final axial advance, then hold. The connector body is at the socket surface; further seating is visually uncertain.
Back off the lip slightly and adjust depth and pitch by a small amount. The plug remains retained, but its stationary base does not establish insertion.
Re-approach with a small depth and lateral correction at the current pitch, using a gentle 1.5 mm descent and preserving the grasp.
Center the plug a fraction of a millimeter left over the visible slot and make a short seating advance, then pause to inspect.
Refine lateral registration with the slot by 0.3 mm and hold without further descent; the connector base is already at the socket surface.
Lift clear of the socket to expose its entrance and the plug tip; repeated contact-level adjustments have not established correct angular alignment.
Use the newly exposed slot to center the plug slightly right, with a small depth correction and a short descent that leaves clearance for inspection.
Approach the exposed slot straight down while slightly reducing the opening target; the plug appears to have shifted upward between the fingers during prior contacts.
Advance the centered plug 1.5 mm along the insertion axis with the adjusted opening, watching whether the body seats or shifts relative to the fingers.
Slightly reduce the opening target and make a one-millimeter seating advance, monitoring the plug relative to the fingers rather than inferring insertion from hand tracking.
Maintain the visibly centered plug and adjusted grasp for a short axial seating advance, then pause; the socket hides the tip, so seating remains uncertain.
Lift the retained connector clear of the lip to inspect its actual tilt and tip alignment; further descent at the same pose has not visibly advanced the body.
Correct the visible cross-slot tilt slightly while above the entrance, compensating laterally to keep the plug tip near the slot center.
Test a modest pitch correction while clear of the socket, compensating hand translation to keep the retained plug tip near the visible entrance.
Approach the exposed entrance at the revised pitch, keeping the plug centered and retained; stop near the lip to assess its motion.
Bring the revised alignment gently to the socket mouth, then pause to inspect whether the connector follows the hand into the opening.
Advance one millimeter along the nearly vertical plug axis, then hold at the socket. Inspect seating before making any further alignment changes.
The plug body is resting at the socket mouth. Keep the hand stationary and gently loosen the fingers to inspect whether the socket supports the connector without further downward sliding.
The released plug remains at the socket but looks tilted. Lift the open fingers slightly to expose its orientation and support before attempting a corrective grasp.
Lower the open fingers around the exposed connector, centering slightly left on its tilted body for a controlled corrective grasp.
Center on the exposed upright connector and close the fingers gradually for a fresh grasp, without pushing it farther into the socket.
The closing fingers visibly tipped the connector instead of securing it squarely. Open and lift slightly to expose its resting orientation before correcting the grasp.
Approach the fallen connector with open fingers, centering slightly right and lowering toward its sides without closing yet.
Position the open pads around the fallen connector's sides, shifting slightly toward the camera and lowering only three millimeters before closing.
Lower the pads slightly alongside the fallen connector and close gradually for a recovery grasp; verify retention visually before lifting far.
Finish closing around the fallen connector and make a short test lift to check whether it is retained between the pads.
The fallen connector did not follow the test lift. Open and move the pads toward its nearer black housing before attempting a lower recovery grasp.
